note:
617 -> 513 -> 517, and the two moves have nothing to do with each other.

The -104 is catalogues catching up with strings that were already reworded, and it was standing at HEAD before this change: `modules` 553 -> 554 and `strings` 8432 -> 8650 moved in the same window, so the tree gained translatable text while the unresolved set shrank. Whoever earned it did not re-floor, so the gate has been red in the falling direction since. Recorded rather than attributed -- the scanner counts strings and not provenance.

The +4 is this change's, and it is the fix working rather than a regression. Every one of the four is a string the extractor could not see before:

  account_journal.py:1360   "...journal of type %s."        was %r
  account_move_line.py:2228 "Journal Item %s created"       was a variable
  account_move_line.py:2384 "Journal Item %s updated"       was a variable
  account_move_line.py:2464 "Journal Item %s deleted"       was a variable

The last three were `_(body_template, link)` -- `_()` given a name rather than a literal, so babel extracted nothing and `account/i18n/` never carried them. Passing the callers' own `_()` call down as a lambda puts the literal back at the call site, which is what `test_gettext_variable` asks for; the %r one is `test_gettext_repr`. A string only becomes unresolved once it is extractable at all, so paying those two findings down necessarily raises this count until the catalogues are exported.

Measured in a detached worktree at HEAD (1df63d05669) carrying this change's files and nothing else: the shared tree also holds another session's in-flight purchase/sale work, and banking that would go red in CI when committed alone. HEAD alone reads 513 there, so the +4 is this change's whole contribution. An exact ratchet fails in the falling direction too, which is why the -104 is banked here rather than left red. The module docstring's MEASURED block is regenerated in the same commit, per its own instruction.
